name: Jedaiah
overview: Jedaiah is a male figure mentioned as one of the exiles who returned from Babylon, as recorded in Zechariah 6:10. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture, and there is some uncertainty about whether he is the same individual as other persons named Jedaiah in the biblical record. This limited information places him within the context of the post-exilic community restoration.
namesAndTitles: The name Jedaiah means 'YHWH has favored' or 'YHWH knows,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's involvement or knowledge. This proper name, as given in Zechariah 6:10, conveys a sense of divine favor or awareness but was not specifically stated to be given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Jedaiah beyond his identification as one of the returning exiles. There are no listed relatives or connections detailed in the biblical text for this individual.
scriptureSignificance: Jedaiah's significance lies in his role as part of the returning exiles who came back from Babylon to rebuild and restore the community of Israel. His mention in Zechariah 6:10 situates him within the prophetic vision concerning the restoration of the priesthood and the temple worship. Although details about his life and lineage are sparse, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of those who returned under God's providence during the post-exilic period.
